violation_type.title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior (26 TAC §744.2103(b)(3))
violation_type.short_title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Redirecting Behavior
violation_type.typical_finding: A carregiver did not use positive statements in the redirection of a child. The caregiver responded to a crying child who was being disciplined by telling him she was "glad that he was crying".  This was corrected at inspection when the person in charge reprimanded the caregiver. The caregiver was sent home due to an inactive background status.

finding_variants.text: A carregiver did not use positive statements in the redirection of a child. The caregiver responded to a crying child who was being disciplined by telling him she was "glad that he was crying".  This was corrected at inspection when the person in charge reprimanded the caregiver. The caregiver was sent home due to an inactive background status.
Based on evidence obtained during the investigation, it was determined that a caregiver pushed a child on his chest as a form of redirection rather than using positive statements.
At the time of the inspection, a caregiver was observed to be using statements such as, "You're working my nerves," and "You're being aggravating" to redirect children.
A caregiver was overheard telling a child they would never have a job again. Positive redirection and behavior expectations were not discussed with the child.
A caregiver did not provide a child with sufficient time or space to redirect, and instead restrained a child on the floor.
A caregiver was not redirecting children in a positive manner and did not use positive statements.
